item.title: Explain Echoes From Scratch

turns.text: Make a 10-second vertical explainer with voice-over about why we hear echoes. Write the words yourself, keep it easy for kids, and choose the look.

item.tests: Tests autonomous short-script writing and delivery of a complete narrated explainer rather than a script-only response.

answer_sheet.Topic and audience: Why we hear echoes, explained simply for kids.

must_haves: One approximately 10-second vertical video includes intelligible English voice-over.
The narration explains that sound reflects off a surface and returns to the listener.
The visuals show sound traveling from a source to a surface and back toward the listener.
The explanation uses simple, child-friendly language and finishes without cutting off the narration.
The visual sound journey and the spoken explanation agree.

turns.text: Could you make an explainer about why we hear echoes? I remember wondering about that as a kid, so it feels like a fun thing to explain. What I have in mind is a 10-second vertical video with a voice-over, and I'd like you to write the words yourself. Please keep the explanation easy for kids to understand. You can choose the look, since I don't have a particular visual style in mind.
turns.agent:
I couldn’t generate the video because your Magic Hour account doesn’t have enough credits. No video was created.

Here’s the ready-to-use **10-second vertical concept**:

**Visual:** A playful cartoon explorer calls toward a distant canyon wall. Glowing sound waves bounce off the rock and return to the explorer’s ear.

**Voice-over:**  
“An echo is your sound coming back! Sound bounces off a faraway wall or mountain, then travels back to your ears.”

Once enough credits are available, I can try generating it again.

approvals.name: create_video_from_text

style.prompt: Create a kid-friendly 10-second vertical educational animation explaining echoes, with bright playful 3D cartoon visuals and clear simple visual storytelling. One continuous wide shot in a sunny canyon: a cheerful cartoon explorer stands at the left foreground facing a distant tall rock wall on the right. The explorer cups a hand beside their mouth; glowing curved sound-wave arcs travel from their mouth across the empty space toward the distant rock wall, visibly bounce off its hard surface, and travel back toward the explorer's ear. The explorer smiles and points to their ear as the waves return. Keep the source person and distant reflecting rock wall visible together, with a clear out-and-back path and no extra scenes. Warm friendly English narrator speaks OFF SCREEN, not lip-synced to the explorer, clearly and naturally with the complete exact narration fitting within ten seconds: "An echo is your sound coming back! Sound bounces off a faraway wall or mountain, then travels back to your ears." Prioritize audible, intelligible voice-over. No on-screen text or captions. Gentle camera push-in, uncluttered composition, cheerful educational mood.
